title: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed
body:
Read the chapter → [Psalms 51](/bible/psalms/51)

This session covers [Psalms 51](/bible/psalms/51) through 54, four chapters of David. [Psalm 51](/bible/psalms/51) is David's prayer of repentance after Nathan the prophet confronted him over Bathsheba and the killing of Uriah. The teaching drives home that Israel must put itself in these scriptures: acknowledge our transgressions, understand what sin is, seek to be cleansed by the word, and know that the wages of sin is the death and captivity we are living in. [Psalms 52](/bible/psalms/52) through 54 turn to the boasting of the wicked man, the fool who says there is no God, and David's cry to be saved from the strangers and oppressors who rise against him.

**[Psalms 51:1](/bible/psalms/51#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/51#v1)</sup> Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

- To the chief musician, a Psalm of David, written after Nathan the prophet came to him following his sin with Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah one of the soldiers in David's army.
- Nathan got on David about it and corrected him. Now David sends up this prayer, asking the Most High for forgiveness.
- David appeals to the loving kindness and tender mercies of the Most High, asking that his transgressions be blotted out.

**[Psalms 51:2](/bible/psalms/51#v2)**
> <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/51#v2)</sup> Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

- David asks to be washed thoroughly from his iniquity and cleansed from his sin. The question is: how are we going to be washed?
  - **[Psalms 119:9](/bible/psalms/119#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/119#v9)</sup> Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.

    We cleanse our ways by taking heed to the word, meaning the Commandments.
  - **[Psalms 119:10](/bible/psalms/119#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/119#v10)</sup> With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments.

    Seek the Most High with the whole heart and ask not to wander from his Commandments; in a world of evil communication we pray that he keep us on the path clean.
  - **[John 15:3](/bible/john/15#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/john/15#v3)</sup> Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.

    We are made clean through the word spoken to us; when we ask to be cleansed we must stand in Christ, abiding in the word to stay on the path of righteousness.

**[Psalms 51:3](/bible/psalms/51#v3)**
> <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/51#v3)</sup> For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.

- David says, "I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me." That is something we must do: acknowledge our transgressions.
- A lot of people do not think we deserve to come over here on slave ships or deserve to be shot down in the streets or deserve the curses put on us. But we sinned against the Most High.
- The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.
  - **[1 Kings 8:46](/bible/1-kings/8#v46)**
    > <sup>[46](/bible/1-kings/8#v46)</sup> If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near;

    There is no man that sinneth not; when Israel sins the Most High delivers them into the hand of the enemy, carried away captive.
  - **[1 Kings 8:33](/bible/1-kings/8#v33)**
    > <sup>[33](/bible/1-kings/8#v33)</sup> When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house:

    When Israel is smitten before the enemy because they have sinned, they must turn again and confess his name.
  - **[Romans 6:23](/bible/romans/6#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/romans/6#v23)</sup> For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

    The wages of sin is death; through sin death came into the world, and our forefathers understood this.
  - **[1 Kings 8:47](/bible/1-kings/8#v47)**
    > <sup>[47](/bible/1-kings/8#v47)</sup> Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;

    In the land of captivity we must bethink ourselves and repent, saying we have sinned and done perversely and committed wickedness.

**[Psalms 51:4](/bible/psalms/51#v4)**
> <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/51#v4)</sup> Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.

- Against the Most High only has David sinned and done this evil in his sight, that the Most High might be justified when he speaks and clear when he judges.
- We are not going to stand before the Most High and be justified talking about "me and Jesus." If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God. Wearing pants, not wearing fringes, crossdressing; none of that will be excused.
  - **[Romans 3:3](/bible/romans/3#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/romans/3#v3)</sup> For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?

    Just because we do not believe does not make the faith of God without effect; our unbelief does not make the Bible untrue.
  - **[Romans 3:4](/bible/romans/3#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/romans/3#v4)</sup> God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.

    Let God be true and every man a liar, as it is written; that is how you speak the word of God.
  - **[Leviticus 5:17](/bible/leviticus/5#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/5#v17)</sup> And if a soul sin, and commit any of these things which are forbidden to be done by the commandments of the Lord; though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

    Sin is when a soul commits any of the things forbidden to be done by the Commandments of the Most High.
  - **[1 John 3:4](/bible/1-john/3#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/1-john/3#v4)</sup> Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.

    Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth the law, for sin is the transgression of the law.

**[Psalms 51:5](/bible/psalms/51#v5)**
> <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/51#v5)</sup> Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.

- David was shapen in iniquity, and in sin did his mother conceive him, meaning he was born from a natural childbirth.

**[Psalms 51:6](/bible/psalms/51#v6)**
> <sup>[6](/bible/psalms/51#v6)</sup> Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.

- The Most High desires truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden part he makes us to know wisdom.

**[Psalms 51:7](/bible/psalms/51#v7)**
> <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/51#v7)</sup> Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

- Purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean; wash me and I shall be whiter than snow. David says this for a reason, because the ordinances set up in the earth are patterned after what goes on in the heavens, and Christ is our high priest.
  - **[Numbers 19:18](/bible/numbers/19#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/numbers/19#v18)</sup> And a clean person shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons that were there, and upon him that touched a bone, or one slain, or one dead, or a grave:

    A clean person takes hyssop, dips it in water, and sprinkles it on the unclean; you had to be clean to do this.
  - **[Numbers 19:19](/bible/numbers/19#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/numbers/19#v19)</sup> And the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day: and on the seventh day he shall purify himself, and wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at even.

    The clean person sprinkles the unclean on the third and seventh day, who then washes his clothes and is clean at evening.

**[Psalms 51:8](/bible/psalms/51#v8)**
> <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/51#v8)</sup> Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.

- Make me to hear joy and gladness, that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice. This does not mean the Most High literally broke his bones; it means correction.
  - **[Psalms 141:5](/bible/psalms/141#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/141#v5)</sup> Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.

    Let the righteous smite me, it shall be a kindness; even the bones broken by correction will rejoice because in the end you get yourself right.

**[Psalms 51:9](/bible/psalms/51#v9)**
> <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/51#v9)</sup> Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.

- Hide thy face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities. Blessed is the man whose transgressions are covered.

**[Psalms 51:10](/bible/psalms/51#v10)**
> <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/51#v10)</sup> Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

- Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.
  - **[2 Esdras 14:34](/bible/2-esdras/14#v34)**
    > <sup>[34](/bible/2-esdras/14#v34)</sup> Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.

    Subdue your own understanding, reform your hearts, and you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.
  - **[Romans 12:2](/bible/romans/12#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/romans/12#v2)</sup> And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

    Be not conformed to this world but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, to prove the good and acceptable will of God.
  - **[2 Corinthians 6:17](/bible/2-corinthians/6#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/2-corinthians/6#v17)</sup> Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,

    Come out of her my people and be ye separate; if you do only what you want to do, you are conformed to this world and your own god.

**[Psalms 51:11](/bible/psalms/51#v11)**
> <sup>[11](/bible/psalms/51#v11)</sup> Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.

- Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy holy spirit from me. The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High.
  - **[Hosea 5:15](/bible/hosea/5#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/hosea/5#v15)</sup> I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.

    The Most High returns to his place until Israel acknowledges their offense and seeks his face in their affliction.
  - **[Lamentations 2:1](/bible/lamentations/2#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/lamentations/2#v1)</sup> How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!

    The Most High cast down the beauty of Israel from heaven to the earth, out of rulership; we have been scattered to the four corners.

**[Psalms 51:12](/bible/psalms/51#v12)**
> <sup>[12](/bible/psalms/51#v12)</sup> Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

- Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit. David understood the importance of losing the kingdom; from the days of John the Baptist the kingdom suffers violence, and they kill us and get away with it. That is the wages of sin.
  - **[2 Esdras 14:13](/bible/2-esdras/14#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/2-esdras/14#v13)</sup> Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption,

    Set thy house in order, reprove thy people, and renounce corruption; David's house was in disarray, and the sword never left it.

**[Psalms 51:13](/bible/psalms/51#v13)**
> <sup>[13](/bible/psalms/51#v13)</sup> Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

- Then will I teach transgressors thy ways, and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

**[Psalms 51:14](/bible/psalms/51#v14)**
> <sup>[14](/bible/psalms/51#v14)</sup> Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.

- Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, because David had killed the man. The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High.
  - **[Genesis 9:5](/bible/genesis/9#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/9#v5)</sup> And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.

    The Most High requires the blood of a man's life at the hand of every man's brother.
  - **[Genesis 9:6](/bible/genesis/9#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/genesis/9#v6)</sup> Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.

    Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man; David was guilty for shedding this man's blood.

**[Psalms 51:15](/bible/psalms/51#v15)**
> <sup>[15](/bible/psalms/51#v15)</sup> O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.

- O Lord, open thou my lips, and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

**[Psalms 51:16](/bible/psalms/51#v16)**
> <sup>[16](/bible/psalms/51#v16)</sup> For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.

- For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.
  - **[1 Samuel 15:22](/bible/1-samuel/15#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/1-samuel/15#v22)</sup> And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

    To obey is better than sacrifice; the Most High delights in obeying his voice more than burnt offerings.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 35:1](/bible/sirach/35#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/sirach/35#v1)</sup> He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.

    He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 35:2](/bible/sirach/35#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/sirach/35#v2)</sup> He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.

    He that taketh heed to the Commandments offereth a peace offering.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 35:3](/bible/sirach/35#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/sirach/35#v3)</sup> To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.

    To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Most High; when you leave sin and repent that is your offering.
  - **[Hebrews 10:8](/bible/hebrews/10#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/hebrews/10#v8)</sup> Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law;

    Sacrifice, offerings, and burnt offerings the Most High would not; he desires obedience.

**[Psalms 51:17](/bible/psalms/51#v17)**
> <sup>[17](/bible/psalms/51#v17)</sup> The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

- The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 3:17](/bible/sirach/3#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/sirach/3#v17)</sup> My son, go on with thy business in meekness; so shalt thou be beloved of him that is approved.

    Go on with thy business in meekness; the greater thou art, the more humble thyself and find favor before the Most High.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 3:19](/bible/sirach/3#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/sirach/3#v19)</sup> Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek.

    Mysteries are revealed unto the meek.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 3:20](/bible/sirach/3#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/sirach/3#v20)</sup> For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.

    For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honored of the lowly.

**[Psalms 51:18](/bible/psalms/51#v18)**
> <sup>[18](/bible/psalms/51#v18)</sup> Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion: build thou the walls of Jerusalem.

- Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion; build thou the walls of Jerusalem. In captivity we are like those who built the wall with one hand and fought with the other; it is time to rebuild a nation.

**[Psalms 51:19](/bible/psalms/51#v19)**
> <sup>[19](/bible/psalms/51#v19)</sup> Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.

- Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering; then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.
